subject: DPA signature plan, subprocessors note, and incident notification timing
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@finovate.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: elena.ortiz@finovate.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA, subprocessors list & timing for signature

Karthik —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached please find the redlined DPA from our side (Finovate_DPA_20261028_redline.pdf). Two items we want to surface before we route to DocuSign:

1) Breach notification timing: our security team needs initial notification "without undue delay" and prefers 24 hours for incidents impacting customer PII.
2) Subprocessors: we need a current export of your subprocessors and a commitment to notify us within 10 business days for new ones.

Can you let us know roughly when Redwood would be able to accept the DPA and whether you prefer us or Redwood to send the DocuSign envelope for signature? If it helps we can circulate the signed DocuSign envelope link when sent.

Attachments: Finovate_DPA_20261028_redline.pdf (redline PDF)

Sam Carter
Head of IT & Security Programs
Finovate Systems
sam.carter@finovate.com

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@finovate.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA, subprocessors list & timing for signature

Sam — thanks for sending this over and for the call. Looping in Dev (legal) and Laura (ops) to review the redline and confirm subprocessors.

Quick answers:
- We can provide a current subprocessors export by EOD tomorrow.
- On DocuSign: either works — we typically route from the vendor side, but we can accept an envelope from you if preferred.

Dev: could you prioritize a read on the redline focused on the breach-notice timing and subprocessors notification windows? Laura: can you prep the subprocessors list and confirm KMS/HSM controls for the docs?

Plan: aim to have a clean DPA for signature by the end of next week, but we may need a short carveout on notice timing.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-29T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA, subprocessors list & timing for signature

Karthik / Laura —

I've reviewed the Finovate redline and attached our internal comments (redwood_internal_comments_20261029.pdf). Key points:

1) Breach notification timing: Finovate's 24-hour ask is aggressive for a global infra provider where we may need to (a) triage, (b) engage forensics, and (c) confirm impact. Proposed compromise: initial notification within 48 hours of discovery for incidents materially impacting Finovate customer data, with a commitment to provide a preliminary summary and a POC contact. Detailed follow-up report within 5 business days or earlier if feasible.

2) Subprocessor notice: we already publish a current subprocessors registry; propose contractual commitment to notify within 10 business days of onboarding a new subprocessor, with an exception for emergency onboarding of critical infra vendors (notice as soon as practicable).

3) Scope/definition edits: tighten "Personal Data" definition to avoid over-broad obligations for telemetry/aggregate metrics.

I've highlighted fallback language to allow for mutual cooperation and to specify that the timing obligations are subject to legal/regulatory disclosure restrictions.

If you want, I can draft a short paragraph replacing Finovate's 24-hour phrasing with our 48-hour/5-day compromise.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@vendorlaw.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Carter <sam.carter@finovate.com>, Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@finovate.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA, subprocessors list & timing for signature

Thanks for the quick review, Dev. Representing Finovate's legal team here. A few clarifications from our side:

- Finovate's security posture requires initial notification within 24 hours for incidents involving unauthorized access to customer PII or credentials. If Redwood is going to push to 48 hours, we need stronger interim commitments: namely, an automated alert to Finovate SOC with summary indicators (scope, suspected vectors, and CISO contact) within 24 hours, and a full incident timeline within 72 hours.

- Regarding subprocessors, Finovate will accept a published registry, but requests a 10-business-day notice for any subprocessor who will have access to decrypted customer content or metadata tied to accounts.

I've attached a short counter-tracking file with specific markup for the breach paragraph (vendor_counsel_countertrack_20261030.docx).

Happy to discuss live tomorrow if useful.

Regards,
Maya Singh
Partner, VendorLaw LLP
maya.singh@vendorlaw.com

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@finovate.com>, Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@finovate.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed sign plan + narrowed redlines

Sam / Elena —

Thanks for the notes, Maya. We've reviewed internally and propose the following path to close quickly:

1) Narrow remaining open items to three bullets only: breach-notice timing language, subprocessor-notice threshold (access to decrypted content), and a small clarification to the Personal Data definition.
2) We're happy to accept a DocuSign envelope from Finovate; please send it to the envelope link below and route in this order: Karthik -> Laura (ops) -> Dev (legal).

DocuSign staging link (if you want to send from your side): https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-FINOVATE

3) Proposed compromise language (suggested by Dev and acceptable to us):
   - Initial notification: within 48 hours of discovery for incidents materially impacting Finovate customer data, with an interim summary sent within 24 hours when possible.
   - Detailed report: within 5 business days of discovery, or earlier where possible; if additional time is needed Redwood will provide a status update and estimated delivery date.

Laura will attach our current subprocessors export once we confirm the envelope routing. If you prefer Redwood to send the envelope instead, say the word and we will initiate from our DocuSign account.

Aim: if we can confirm routing today, we can execute the agreement by mid-week.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@finovate.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Carter <sam.carter@finovate.com>, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed sign plan + narrowed redlines

Karthik / team —

Confirming we've sent and completed the DocuSign envelope. Attached is the fully executed DPA (Finovate_DPA_signed_20261102.pdf).

Regarding breach notification, we accept Redwood's compromise language as follows:
- Initial notification: within 48 hours of discovery for incidents materially impacting Finovate customer data; if possible, an interim summary to Finovate SOC within 24 hours.
- Detailed investigation report: within 7 business days (we agreed to 7 business days in the final text to align with our internal incident review cadence).

Per subprocessors, we reviewed Redwood's published registry and Finovate will require 10 business days' notice for new subprocessors that will access decrypted customer content.

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Sam and I will route this to procurement and legal for internal filing.

Best,
Elena Ortiz
Procurement & Vendor Governance
Finovate Systems
elena.ortiz@finovate.com

[Attachment: Finovate_DPA_signed_20261102.pdf]
